rules.sentence: Actinic keratosis can present in various forms, such as scaly, erythematous macules, papules, plaques, or cutaneous horns.
The evaluation of actinic keratosis is primarily based on clinical observation during the physical examination.
However, additional diagnostic techniques such as dermoscopy or biopsy may provide valuable information in certain cases.
Nonpigmented facial actinic keratoses may exhibit a “strawberry pattern.”
This pattern includes an erythematous vessel pseudo network, prominent follicular openings, and a surrounding white halo.[7]
